Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business coverage is dominated by Anthropic's record-breaking IPO pricing and Nvidia's first earnings report since Jensen Huang's ouster, with outlets also converging on the New York Times' DealBook Summit, growing worries about an AI credit/valuation bubble, and a batch of strong retail earnings (Target, Lowe's, Home Depot).

stories.headline: Anthropic prices record-breaking IPO amid AI jitters
stories.summary: Anthropic is pricing what could be the largest IPO ever, with bankers briefing that the deal is close to seven times oversubscribed and guiding toward the top of its $70-78 range or above, even as tech stocks have churned on AI-bubble fears.

stories.headline: Nvidia's strong earnings ease AI jitters but questions linger post-Huang
stories.summary: Nvidia's quarterly results and forward guidance helped halt a days-long tech-stock selloff and reassured investors the company can thrive without Jensen Huang, though deeper questions about its future remain unresolved.

stories.headline: NYT's DealBook Summit convenes Vance, Musk, Altman amid AI and political uncertainty
stories.summary: The 2026 DealBook Summit arrives amid concern over the sustainability of the AI rally and a midterm election that reshuffled Washington's balance of power, with JD Vance, Elon Musk, Sam Altman and other major figures on the lineup.

stories.headline: Credit chiefs and ECB warn AI buildout echoes subprime-era risks
stories.summary: The European Central Bank has raised concerns that hyperscalers are amassing trillions of dollars in off-balance-sheet commitments through interlocking tech contracts, drawing comparisons to the subprime bubble.

stories.headline: Target and Lowe's post strong results and raise guidance
stories.summary: Target posted its best sales growth in five years and raised guidance as its turnaround effort continues, while Lowe's also raised its outlook on strong online sales despite a sluggish housing market.

stories.headline: Fed's Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House firing hearing
stories.summary: Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook will not participate in a December 14 White House hearing on whether to fire her unless the panel and its rules are changed, her lawyer said, citing bias.

stories.headline: U.S. could hit debt limit by February
stories.summary: The Bipartisan Policy Center estimates the United States will soon run up against its statutory debt ceiling, adding a fresh fiscal flashpoint in Washington.

stories.headline: Rush to patch AI-discovered bugs blamed for wave of tech outages
stories.summary: Experts say a rush to fix software flaws that were found by AI tools likely created the instability behind recent outages at Microsoft, JPMorgan, the FAA and other major institutions.

Business.gaps: Puck had no business-relevant items surfaced in search; The Economist, Politico, BBC, WSJ, NYT, and FT were covered only via feed items and limited search since they block broader search access.

US politics.overview: Coverage is dominated by the aftermath of Democrats' sweeping midterm Senate takeover (capped by Mary Peltola's Alaska win) and Trump's high-stakes Asia trip featuring a historic Xi-Putin-Trump trilateral in Shenzhen. Beltway outlets are also fixated on an intensifying Senate Democratic leadership fight, House Democrats gearing up for Trump-family investigations, fallout from Nvidia's Jensen Huang scandal fueling new China chip legislation, and a contentious $50 billion FAA funding request in the lame-duck session.

stories.headline: Peltola flips Alaska, giving Democrats a 56-seat Senate majority
stories.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan in Alaska, the last race called this cycle, giving Democrats a 56-44 Senate edge and capping a historic sweep of nine flipped seats.

stories.headline: Xi greets Trump on tarmac as trilateral summit with Putin opens in Shenzhen
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping broke diplomatic protocol to personally greet and hug Trump upon arrival in Shenzhen ahead of a rare trilateral meeting with Putin at the APEC summit, with Xi and Putin both publicly condemning U.S. sanctions beforehand.

stories.headline: Schumer-Van Hollen Senate leadership brawl heats up ahead of vote
stories.summary: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer faces an unexpected challenge from Sen. Chris Van Hollen, with Schumer currently holding a 15-5 lead in public endorsements as he pushes a 2027 agenda built around lowering costs and ending corruption.

stories.headline: White House moves to restrict staff testimony as House Dems ramp up Trump-family probes
stories.summary: A White House Counsel memo now requires agencies to get sign-off before any employee testifies to Congress, a move Axios says is aimed at blunting the sweeping investigations into Trump allies and family that incoming House Democratic majorities, led by Rep. Robert Garcia, are preparing to launch.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang scandal supercharges China chip-crackdown push in Congress
stories.summary: With Huang out as Nvidia CEO and Commerce Secretary Lutnick facing scrutiny, congressional China hawks say three export-control bills aimed at curbing chip sales to China are closer than ever to passing, likely attached to the defense policy bill.

stories.headline: Duffy's $50 billion FAA overhaul request hits GOP resistance
stories.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's $50 billion air-traffic-control funding request is getting a chilly reception from Senate Republicans, who are balking at the price tag even after last week's nationwide ground stop.

stories.headline: Fed Governor Lisa Cook refuses to attend White House firing hearing
stories.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook's lawyer said she won't participate in a December White House hearing on whether to remove her unless the panel and its rules are changed, citing bias.

stories.headline: Supreme Court takes up mandatory detention and asylum ban cases
stories.summary: SCOTUSblog reports the justices are confronting a cluster of immigration disputes, including mandatory detention policy and a newly granted asylum ban case, alongside continued scrutiny of the administration's reliance on the emergency docket.

US politics.gaps: The Guardian, NYT, National Review, Washington Examiner, Fox News, WSJ, Courthouse News, Stateline, The Dispatch, and RealClearPolitics block direct search, so coverage for those outlets reflects only the feed items supplied, not independent verification.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and business outlets is dominated by the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation as Nvidia CEO, including the chipmaker's reassuring earnings, its decision to halt AI chip sales to China, and a new SEC probe, alongside the climactic pricing of Anthropic's blockbuster IPO. Secondary threads include fresh AI model releases (OpenAI's GPT-6.2, Alibaba's Qwen4-Max), tightening US export controls on China, and growing scrutiny of AI infrastructure spending and its societal effects.

stories.headline: Nvidia reassures markets with strong earnings despite Huang's exit
stories.summary: Nvidia projected its record revenue streak would continue even after the departure of founder Jensen Huang, a message that helped calm a multi-day tech stock selloff.

stories.headline: Nvidia halts advanced AI chip sales to China
stories.summary: Nvidia has stopped shipping advanced AI chips to China despite earlier White House approval, with TechCrunch reporting the interim CEO says the company is done selling to the market following Huang's ouster.

stories.headline: SEC opens civil probe into Nvidia over undisclosed China chip sales
stories.summary: The SEC has launched a civil investigation into Nvidia tied to chip sales in China that weren't disclosed, adding to the company's post-Huang turmoil, with WSJ noting the probe alongside slower retail sales data.

stories.headline: Anthropic nears pricing on what could be history's biggest IPO
stories.summary: Anthropic is on the cusp of pricing its IPO, defying a tech stock selloff, with Bloomberg reporting the company was guiding bankers toward the top of its $70-$78 share range or above amid heavy investor demand.

stories.headline: US moves to close loophole letting China access AI compute via third countries
stories.summary: Washington is tightening export controls so data centers in countries like Singapore and Malaysia need a US license to buy Nvidia chips, though The Decoder reports China has already built a parallel AI supply chain to route around the restrictions.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
stories.summary: OpenAI's company announcement introduces two new models with better professional outputs, coding, and computer-use capability at lower prices across ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API; The Decoder reports Astra ranks second behind Claude in independent benchmarks.

stories.headline: ECB warns AI borrowing binge echoes subprime-era risk
stories.summary: The FT reports concerns that hyperscalers are building up trillions of dollars in off-balance-sheet commitments through contracts with other tech firms, which the ECB says has "historic parallels" with the subprime bubble.

stories.headline: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion in second mega-round within six months
stories.summary: Alphabet's AI drug discovery company, led by Demis Hassabis, raised $5 billion just six months after a $2.1 billion round to push forward its research pipeline.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer and Rest of World had no stories from the last 48 hours; their most recent relevant pieces were over a week old. The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and The Guardian were assessed only via the provided feed items and VentureBeat/Platformer/Rest of World/The Information/Anthropic/Google DeepMind searches, since some of these outlets block direct web search verification.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging on fallout from the U.S. midterms for data-center and utility investment, a wave of fossil-fuel M&A, and the Trump administration's continued moves to prop up coal and gas generation. Geopolitical risk to energy supply is also prominent, with Iran's escalation in the Strait of Hormuz and new scrutiny of historical CO2 exporters ahead of COP31.

stories.headline: Iran escalates Strait of Hormuz conflict, striking Kuwait and Bahrain
stories.summary: Iran has widened its confrontation over the Strait of Hormuz by striking targets in Kuwait and Bahrain, following an earlier attack on a natural gas tanker in the strait, as a quiet U.S. military response reportedly continues.

stories.headline: Trump administration issues seventh emergency order to keep Michigan coal plant running
stories.summary: The Department of Energy has again invoked Federal Power Act emergency authority to keep the coal-fired J.H. Campbell plant in Michigan operating past its planned retirement, citing reliability concerns on the Midwest grid.

stories.headline: NRG Energy to sell 4.9 GW of gas plants to LS Power for $4 billion
stories.summary: NRG Energy is offloading nearly 5 gigawatts of gas-fired generation to LS Power even as it simultaneously develops new gas capacity in Texas, highlighting active portfolio reshuffling among power generators amid surging demand.

stories.headline: Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia revealed as history's largest CO2 exporters
stories.summary: A new Carbon Brief analysis finds Russia, Saudi Arabia and Australia have cumulatively exported more carbon dioxide than any other nations in history, a pointed finding given Australia's role as incoming COP31 co-president.

stories.headline: Data center slowdown threatens billions in planned utility investment
stories.summary: An estimated 191 gigawatts of planned data center capacity faces new risk following the midterm elections, with exposure concentrated in Texas, Ohio and Georgia, raising questions about utilities' infrastructure bets.

stories.headline: Nvidia's sprawling investments tie it closely to energy and climate startups
stories.summary: Heatmap details how Nvidia and its venture arm have become major financial backers of nuclear, grid-software, geothermal and storage startups, raising questions about what happens to that funding pipeline as AI investment comes under scrutiny.

Energy.gaps: Argus Media could not be searched within the allotted search budget, so no recent coverage is reported. E&E News search results returned only older archived stories with nothing from the last 48 hours. Reuters, FT and The Economist block web search and had no relevant feed items provided, so no current coverage from them could be reported.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across China-focused outlets is dominated by the first-ever Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral summit at APEC in Shenzhen, alongside the broader diplomatic choreography of the APEC Leaders' Meeting (Japan, Canada, Mexico and other bilaterals). A secondary cluster of stories covers the deepening US-China tech fight over AI chip access following the Nvidia scandal, and signs of continued softness in China's domestic economy even as EV and tech sectors keep churning out announcements.

stories.headline: Xi, Trump and Putin hold historic trilateral summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin held the first-ever face-to-face trilateral summit among the three countries' leaders on the sidelines of the APEC Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, with Xi greeting Trump on the tarmac in a reciprocal gesture after Trump's own airport welcome for him in Washington, and Putin appearing in the APEC "family photo" for the first time in nine years, positioned centrally between Xi and Trump. State-run Global Times hailed the summit as proof that China's major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics is entering a new phase and a sign of international recognition of China's stable image, while SCMP noted comparisons to the 1945 Yalta Conference have unsettled observers given how that meeting once carved up postwar spheres of influence.

stories.headline: US tightens curbs on China's indirect access to advanced AI chips
stories.summary: Washington moved to close loopholes that let Chinese firms obtain advanced AI chips via overseas data centers, with new rules targeting data centers in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia in the wake of the Nvidia espionage scandal. Taipei Times' front page flagged the same move, while Hong Kong Free Press reported Singapore is in damage control as the episode exposed how Chinese companies allegedly used the city-state as a loophole to reach top-end chips.

stories.headline: China's economy softens as factory output and retail sales slow
stories.summary: China's economy continues to grapple with sluggish domestic demand even as it is buoyed by robust technology exports, with key economic bellwethers showing signs of weakness in October. The People's Bank of China separately hiked the foreign reserve requirement ratio for the first time in five years, a move aimed at strengthening foreign exchange liquidity management for financial institutions as policymakers guard against yuan appreciation.

stories.headline: China's NEV retail sales fall 13% in early November
stories.summary: China's new-energy vehicle retail sales totaled 447,000 units in the first 15 days of November, down 13% and lagging total passenger vehicle sales of 611,000 units, even as NEV penetration reached 73.2% of the market.

stories.headline: Xi and Takaichi have first in-person interaction since Japan-China freeze
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Xi Jinping had their first in-person interaction in Shenzhen since ties froze last autumn over her remarks on Taiwan, with Bloomberg reporting Xi shook hands with Takaichi on Wednesday in the first official interaction between the two leaders since bilateral ties deteriorated.

stories.headline: China building new South China Sea island runway, analysts say
stories.summary: Satellite imagery and analyst assessments indicate China is building a runway on another disputed South China Sea island, a move experts say could significantly bolster Beijing's military footprint in the strategic waterway.

stories.headline: Xi calls for global association linking bay-area tech hubs
stories.summary: Xi Jinping proposed closer economic links between major coastal innovation centers worldwide, from Shenzhen to Silicon Valley, with observers saying the plan could open new opportunities for exchange between global tech hubs.

stories.headline: Russian warplanes enter Taiwan's air defense identification zone
stories.summary: Taipei Times reported that Russian warplanes entered Taiwan's air defense identification zone, adding a new dimension to regional security tensions during the same week as the Shenzhen summit.

China.gaps: No recent (last 48h) items were found via search for Caixin Global, Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, Yicai Global or Focus Taiwan; coverage for Reuters, AP, NYT and The Economist relies only on the feed items provided since these outlets block direct search.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the rapidly escalating US-Iran conflict, with Iran striking Kuwait and Bahrain after US jets hit Iran's Qeshm Island, sending oil prices toward record highs and prompting widespread Gulf condemnation. Israeli outlets are absorbed by a parliamentary power shift as a new, anti-Netanyahu Knesset speaker moves to roll back the outgoing premier's legacy, while other outlets track Gaza ceasefire strains, a new US-Saudi nuclear deal, and a Somalia-UAE diplomatic row.

stories.headline: Iran strikes Kuwait and Bahrain after US hits Qeshm Island
stories.summary: Iran targeted Kuwait's Ali Al Salem air base and launched fresh drone attacks on Bahrain after US fighter jets struck an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island, with Gulf states condemning the 'hostile' escalation and a crew member still missing after an Adnoc tanker was hit in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Hormuz disruption pushes oil and sulphur prices to record highs
stories.summary: Adnoc expects sulphur output to double as the prolonged Strait of Hormuz disruption drives related commodity prices to record levels, underscoring how the Iran war is reshaping Gulf energy markets even as AGBI reports oil has stayed well below the $200 'worst-case' fears despite mounting Hormuz attacks.

stories.headline: Israel's new Knesset speaker moves to unwind Netanyahu's legacy
stories.summary: Israel's parliament convened under newly elected speaker Matan Kahana of the anti-Netanyahu Eisenkot bloc, which is now pushing legislation to repeal elements of the outgoing government's judicial overhaul, while Netanyahu allies called the speaker's election elected with Arab-party votes an 'eternal disgrace.'

stories.headline: IAEA calls new US-Saudi civil nuclear deal 'satisfactory'
stories.summary: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi welcomed the newly announced US-Saudi agreement to equip the kingdom with a civilian nuclear program, a significant milestone for Gulf energy diplomacy amid the broader regional conflict.

stories.headline: Trump's Board of Peace says Gaza ceasefire has achieved 'nothing visible'
stories.summary: The body overseeing Trump's Gaza plan accused both Israel and Hamas of failing to meet their ceasefire commitments, as Israeli tanks reportedly pushed into residential areas near Bureij and Nuseirat and strikes killed three more Palestinians, including a child.

stories.headline: Somalia's president accuses UAE of 'interference'
stories.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud used a televised address to accuse the UAE of interfering in Somalia's internal affairs, alleging Gulf-funded armed groups, opening a new diplomatic rift between Mogadishu and Abu Dhabi.

stories.headline: Saudi banks shift funding model as loans expand and deposits move
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's banking sector is navigating a new funding equation as loan growth outpaces and reshapes deposit patterns, a trend being closely watched as the kingdom pursues large-scale economic diversification projects.

stories.headline: Bahrain's war-hit Sitra refinery weeks from full capacity
stories.summary: Bapco Energies' CEO said Bahrain's Sitra refinery, damaged amid the regional conflict, is weeks away from returning to full operating capacity, a sign of the war's lingering toll on Gulf energy infrastructure.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Khaleej Times, Arabian Business, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, and Reuters/AP/FT/NYT/The Economist/BBC yielded no distinct recent items beyond what overlapped with other outlets' coverage of the Iran-Gulf escalation.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Africa coverage over the past 48 hours clusters around high-stakes diplomacy and security (Western Sahara's escalating standoff as UN peacekeepers withdraw, the Rwanda-EU deportation scheme, and a Nigeria-South Africa diplomatic spat), alongside notable business and mining developments including a major African tech expansion and mining-sector corporate moves in the DRC and Angola. South African coalition politics after local elections also features prominently.

stories.headline: Zipline taps Uber veteran to lead major African drone-delivery expansion
stories.summary: As Uber scales back its African ride-hailing footprint, drone delivery firm Zipline has hired an Uber expansion veteran, Anthony le Roux, to lead its African operations and oversee plans for at least 20 new drone hubs over two years.

stories.headline: Western Sahara tensions escalate as Polisario mobilises and UN peacekeepers leave
stories.summary: The Polisario Front has called for mobilisation against Morocco just as the UN peacekeeping mission to the territory has not been renewed, raising questions about the ageing Sahrawi movement's military capacity and the risk of a wider flare-up.

stories.headline: Fears grow over EU-Rwanda migrant deportation scheme
stories.summary: A five-nation European plan to send migrants to a Rwandan 'welcome centre' with residence permits is drawing criticism from rights groups who fear it could become a broader deportation model; Al Jazeera reports lawyers, journalists and politicians are calling the arrangement inhumane.

stories.headline: Nigeria's envoy softens tone after clash with South African presidency
stories.summary: Nigeria's new high commissioner to South Africa picked a public fight with Pretoria's presidency within hours of presenting his credentials, prompting a summons from South Africa's foreign ministry that has tempered, but not ended, bilateral doubts.

stories.headline: Angola seeks 10% stake in De Beers amid Anglo American's exit
stories.summary: Angola is seeking a 10% holding in De Beers as part of Anglo American's proposed sale of its stake in the major diamond producer, a mines ministry spokesperson told Reuters.

stories.headline: Senegal's budget defeat puts $2.2bn IMF rescue in jeopardy
stories.summary: Bond investors are punishing Dakar as a political feud between the president and a former premier stalls the debt overhaul tied to Senegal's IMF programme, according to the outlet's latest issue.

stories.headline: Mashaba emerges as coalition kingmaker after South African local elections
stories.summary: ActionSA leader Herman Mashaba has become pivotal to coalition negotiations for both the ANC and the DA in Gauteng following local elections, though his demand over the DA's Helen Zille complicates talks.

Africa.gaps: No direct, dated feed items were available for AP, Reuters, BBC, FT, NYT, or WSJ (these outlets block search, so only items appearing in Mining Weekly's own reporting, which attributes some stories to Reuters and Bloomberg, could be used). The Continent's website showed only archived back issues rather than fresh items from the last 48 hours.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage this cycle centers on labor tensions over AI and pay at Reuters, a marquee morning-show talent shuffle tied to the NBC-MS NOW split, and continued scrutiny of press freedom abroad. Trade press is also tracking corporate restructuring in cable/streaming and advertising-tech turbulence, while niche outlets like CJR and Press Gazette dig into AI's encroachment on journalism itself.

stories.headline: Reuters journalists authorize strike over AI protections and wages
stories.summary: An overwhelming majority of unionized Reuters journalists in the U.S. voted to authorize a strike after more than a year of stalled contract talks over wages, AI protections and manager overreach, with one correspondent noting Reuters is profitable and can afford to pay more.

stories.headline: Willie Geist to leave MS NOW's 'Morning Joe' for expanded NBC 'Today' role
stories.summary: Willie Geist is exiting MS NOW's 'Morning Joe' after nearly two decades alongside Joe Scarborough and Mika Brzezinski to focus full-time on NBC's 'Today' franchise, ending the last dual-network arrangement left over from the NBCU-Versant split; Status reports the move capped months of behind-the-scenes negotiations.

stories.headline: Costa Rican journalist shot dead in first such killing in 25 years
stories.summary: Camilo Rodríguez, a journalist known for publishing allegations against suspected drug traffickers, was shot dead as Costa Rica faces a surge in drug-related violence, marking the country's first such killing in a quarter-century.

stories.headline: Egypt brings court case against Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah
stories.summary: CJR profiles Lina Attalah, editor of Egypt's leading independent outlet Mada Masr, who is being prosecuted by the Egyptian government even as she remains hopeful; she says simply that 'journalism cannot breathe' under the crackdown.

stories.headline: Daily Mail joins publisher coalition fighting AI news scrapers
stories.summary: The Daily Mail has joined a coalition of publishers pushing back against AI scraping of news content, with the group set to play what Press Gazette describes as 'a major role' in shaping industry rules for AI use.

stories.headline: Skydance restructures cable programming after Warner Bros-Paramount merger
stories.summary: Skydance has formed Skydance Global Cable Media, naming four executives to oversee more than 50 cable brands including MTV, BET, Comedy Central and Discovery as it folds together the former Warner Bros Discovery and Paramount cable units, with one longtime executive exiting.

stories.headline: Wachowskis move to reclaim 'The Matrix' rights from Warner Bros
stories.summary: Puck reports that filmmakers Lana and Lilly Wachowski have formally notified Warner Bros. they are exercising copyright termination rights to reclaim 'The Matrix' franchise, setting up high-stakes negotiations just as a fifth film is in development under David Ellison's Skydance.

stories.headline: The Trade Desk loses three senior executives amid first revenue decline since 2020
stories.summary: The ad-tech firm The Trade Desk is losing leaders in engineering, client service and commercial operations as it grapples with its first revenue decline since 2020.

Media.gaps: NYT, WSJ and FT block web search and had no relevant media-industry feed items provided beyond general Iran/markets coverage, so their current media-beat coverage could not be assessed.
